paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: : labelformat=parens, labelsep=period
model_annotation: The figure titled “GPT2-XL” illustrates how two metrics, **Efficacy\_top** and **noise\_E**, vary across the same sequence of x-values for two methods (AlphaEdit and DeltaEdit), with efficacy shown on the left y-axis and noise on the right y-axis. The x-axis has no visible label and uses a linear scale; plotted points occur at approximately 250, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, and 3000, with numeric tick labels shown at 500-unit intervals from 500 to 3000. The left y-axis is labeled **Efficacy\_top**, spans roughly 86 to 100 on a linear scale, and shows evenly spaced tick labels every 2 units (86, 88, …, 100). The right y-axis is labeled **noise\_E**, spans roughly 2 to 12 on a linear scale, and shows tick labels every 2 units (2, 4, …, 12). Four lines are plotted: **AlphaEdit Efficacy\_top** is a red dashed line with square markers that starts near ~99.4 at x≈250, stays near ~99 through x≈1000, then declines to ~97.4 at x≈1500, ~95.8 at x≈2000, ~92.1 at x≈2500, and ends near ~85.9 at x≈3000; **DeltaEdit Efficacy\_top** is a purple dashed line with square markers that starts near ~99.5 at x≈250, decreases gradually to ~99.2 (x≈500) and ~99.0 (x≈1000), then to ~98.0 (x≈1500), ~97.0 (x≈2000), ~95.8 (x≈2500), and ends near ~93.8 at x≈3000. **AlphaEdit noise\_E** is a red solid line with circular markers that increases from about ~2.7 at x≈250 to ~4.3 (x≈500), ~6.5 (x≈1000), ~7.8 (x≈1500), ~9.2 (x≈2000), ~10.4 (x≈2500), and ~11.8 at x≈3000. **DeltaEdit noise\_E** is a purple solid line with circular markers that also rises, from about ~2.4 at x≈250 to ~4.3 (x≈500), ~6.5 (x≈1000), ~7.8 (x≈1500), ~9.1 (x≈2000), ~10.2 (x≈2500), and ~11.2 at x≈3000.
